newsitem.title: USA: Red Lobster to get new look, lower prices.
newsitem.headline: Red Lobster to get new look, lower prices.

text.p: Red Lobster, the nation's largest seafood restaurant chain, said Tuesday it will spend $150 million to redecorate its more than 600 outlets and cut its prices.
The Darden Restaurants Inc. subsidiary said it will also drop prices, add new entrees and increase its portions.
More than 75 percent of Red Lobster restaurants will have a "new wharfside look" within the next year, the company said.
Red Lobster also said it was dropping its prices and increasing the size of its food portions.
Fifteen of Red Lobster's entrees are now priced under $10, the company said. The new items were launched Monday.

"We've dropped our prices because we want our customers to be able to visit us more often -- not to think of dining at Red Lobster as a special occasion," said Jeff O'Hara, Chief Operating Officer, Red Lobster. "This everyday pricing is possible since we have moved away from couponing."
The stock of Orlando, Fla.-based Darden rose 37.5 cents to $8.75 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
